derivations.claim: Since $\mathcal F_\sigma=d\mathcal A_\sigma$, the identity $d^2=0$ in [F5] gives $d\mathcal F_\sigma=0$. Raising the two indices of $\mathcal F_{i0}=-\sigma H_i/H^2$ with [F2] gives $\mathcal F^{i0}=\sigma H_i/H^2$ and $\mathcal F^{0i}=-\sigma H_i/H^2$. Contracting the antisymmetric pair yields $\mathcal F_{ab}\mathcal F^{ab}=2\sum_i\mathcal F_{i0}\mathcal F^{i0}=-2q_H/H^4$.

The last Christoffel term in $\nabla_a\mathcal F^{ab}=\partial_a\mathcal F^{ab}+\Gamma^a{}_{ac}\mathcal F^{cb}+\Gamma^b{}_{ac}\mathcal F^{ac}$ vanishes because $\Gamma^b{}_{ac}$ is symmetric in $a,c$ and $\mathcal F^{ac}$ is antisymmetric. For $b=0$, the remaining terms are $\partial_i(\sigma H_i/H^2)+(2H_i/H)(\sigma H_i/H^2)=\sigma\Delta_\delta H/H^2=0$, after the product rule cancels the two $q_H/H^3$ terms. For $b=i$, $\partial_0\mathcal F^{0i}=0$, all $\mathcal F^{ji}=0$, and the only possible trace term is $\Gamma^\alpha{}_{\alpha0}\mathcal F^{0i}=0$. Thus $v^b=\nabla_a\mathcal F^{ab}=0$ for every $b$, and [F4] gives $d(\star_g\mathcal F_\sigma)=0$.

The only nonzero contraction in $\mathcal F_{0c}\mathcal F_0{}^c$ is $\sum_iF_{0i}F_0{}^i=q_H/H^6$, while $\mathcal F_{ic}\mathcal F_j{}^c=F_{i0}g^{00}F_{j0}=-H_iH_j/H^2$. Combining these with $\mathcal F_{ab}\mathcal F^{ab}=-2q_H/H^4$ and $g_{00}=-H^{-2}$, $g_{ij}=H^2\delta_{ij}$ gives $Q_{00}=q_H/(2H^6)$, $Q_{0i}=0$, and $Q_{ij}=(\delta_{ij}q_H-2H_iH_j)/(2H^2)$.

Substituting $\Delta_\delta H=0$ into the arbitrary-positive-$H$ table [F3] gives $\operatorname{Ric}_{00}=q_H/H^6$, $\operatorname{Ric}_{0i}=0$, and $\operatorname{Ric}_{ij}=(\delta_{ij}q_H-2H_iH_j)/H^2$. These are exactly twice the entries in step 2.2; together with the closedness in step 1.1 and source-free divergence in step 2.1 they are all three equations in [[def-emg-xs-geometric-electrovac]].

derivations.claim: For $z\ne0$, direct differentiation gives $\partial_i|z|^{-1}=-z_i|z|^{-3}$ and $\partial_i^2|z|^{-1}=-|z|^{-3}+3z_i^2|z|^{-5}$. Summing over $i$ yields $\Delta_\delta|z|^{-1}=-3|z|^{-3}+3|z|^2|z|^{-5}=0$. Every term in $H$ is smooth on $D$, and every term is positive there, so $H>0$ and $\Delta_\delta H=0$ on $D$.

Inverting the diagonal metric in [F1] gives $g^{00}=-H^2$ and $g^{ij}=H^{-2}\delta^{ij}$, so raising $\mathcal F_{i0}=-\sigma H_i/H^2$ gives $\mathcal F^{i0}=\sigma H_i/H^2$. The metric determinant is $(-H^{-2})(H^2)^3=-H^4$, so the oriented volume form is $\mathrm{vol}_g=H^2dx^0\wedge dx^1\wedge dx^2\wedge dx^3$. The Hodge formula [F4] therefore gives $(\star_g\mathcal F_\sigma)_{ij}=-\sigma\epsilon_{ijk}H_k$. Evaluating this two-form on an outward-oriented Euclidean sphere gives $\int_S\star_g\mathcal F_\sigma=-\sigma\int_S\partial_\nu H\,dS_\delta$, because $\partial_\nu H=n^kH_k$ and the induced oriented area form has components $\epsilon_{ijk}n^k dS_\delta$. The pullback of $\mathcal F_\sigma$ to each spatial sphere is zero because every term in [F1] contains $dx^0$, which vanishes on its tangent vectors; hence $q_m(S)=0$.

Let $S_r(a)$ be a Euclidean sphere with center $a$ and radius $r$, and let $m/|x-b|$ be one term in $H$, where $d:=|b-a|\ne r$. At $x=a+rn$ with $n\in S^2$, its outward normal derivative is $-m(r-n\cdot(b-a))/|rn-(b-a)|^3$. The sphere area element is $r^2d\Omega$, where $d\Omega=\sin\theta\,d\theta\,d\phi$ and $\int_{S^2}d\Omega=2\pi\int_0^\pi\sin\theta\,d\theta=4\pi$. If $d=0$, direct integration gives flux $-4\pi m$. If $d>0$, choose the polar axis along $b-a$; this orthogonal change preserves the induced sphere area. With $u=\cos\theta$ and $n\cdot(b-a)=du$, the flux is $-2\pi mr^2J$, where $$J:=\int_{-1}^{1}\frac{r-du}{(r^2+d^2-2rdu)^{3/2}}\,du.$$ Set $w=r^2+d^2-2rdu$. Then $du=-dw/(2rd)$, the endpoint square roots for $w$ are $r+d$ and $|r-d|$, and $r-du=(r^2-d^2+w)/(2r)$. Therefore $$J=\frac1{4r^2d}\left((r^2-d^2)\int_{(r-d)^2}^{(r+d)^2}w^{-3/2}\,dw+\int_{(r-d)^2}^{(r+d)^2}w^{-1/2}\,dw\right).$$ Using antiderivatives $-2w^{-1/2}$ and $2w^{1/2}$ gives $$J=\frac{(r^2-d^2)\bigl(|r-d|^{-1}-(r+d)^{-1}\bigr)+(r+d-|r-d|)}{2r^2d}.$$ If $d<r$, the numerator is $4d$, so $J=2/r^2$; if $d>r$, the numerator is $0$, so $J=0$. Thus a Coulomb term contributes $-4\pi m$ to the outward flux exactly when its center lies inside the sphere, and zero when its center lies outside.
The conditions in [F1] now hold, so the defined data exist on the entire punctured domain. Applying [F2] proves the source-free field equations there; no equation is asserted at a removed center.

For an isolated sphere $S_A(r)$, its own center has $d=0$, while each other center has distance $d_{AB}>r$ by [A1]. Applying step 1.3 term by term gives $\int_{S_A(r)}\partial_\nu H\,dS_\delta=-4\pi m_A$. Step 1.2 yields $q_e(S_A(r))=\sigma m_A$, and that step also gives $q_m(S_A(r))=0$.

Let $D\subseteq\mathbb R^3$ be open and let $H\in C^\infty(D,(0,\infty))$ be independent of time. Write $x=(x^1,x^2,x^3)$ for length coordinates, set $x^0=ct$ when a time variable is used, and require $H$ to be dimensionless. The ordinary Euclidean Laplacian is $\Delta_\delta H:=\sum_{i=1}^3\partial_i^2H$; call $H$ harmonic when $\Delta_\delta H=0$. Take $\mathcal M=\mathbb R_{x^0}\times D$, with orientation $dx^0\wedge dx^1\wedge dx^2\wedge dx^3$ and future direction selected by $N_H=H\partial_{x^0}$.

For a sign $\sigma\in\{-1,+1\}$ define the metric and global potential one-form

$$g_H=-H^{-2}(dx^0)^2+H^2\sum_{i=1}^3(dx^i)^2,\qquad \mathcal A_\sigma=\sigma(H^{-1}-1)\,dx^0.$$

The associated two-form is

$$\mathcal F_\sigma:=d\mathcal A_\sigma=-\sigma\sum_{i=1}^3\frac{H_i}{H^2}\,dx^i\wedge dx^0,\qquad H_i:=\partial_iH.$$

The **positive harmonic conformastatic electrovac data** are the tuple $(\mathcal M,g_H,N_H,o,\mathcal F_\sigma)$ for these choices. The metric is the chart tensor of [[def-emg-conformastatic-chart-data]] and is Lorentzian with the stated future direction by [[lem-emg-conformastatic-chart-is-lorentzian]]. The term “electrovac data” names a candidate for the equations in [[def-emg-xs-geometric-electrovac]]; this definition by itself does not assert that the equations hold. The field components have inverse-length units in length coordinates, so the Ricci and quadratic-field components both have inverse-length-squared units.

Let $M,q_e,q_m\in\mathbb R$ be length parameters and put
$Q^2:=q_e^2+q_m^2$. Let $J\subset(0,\infty)$ be open and require
$$f(r):=1-\frac{2M}{r}+\frac{Q^2}{r^2}\ne0\qquad(r\in J).$$
On the smooth product $\mathcal M_J:=\mathbb R_{x^0}\times J_r\times S^2$,
let $\gamma_{S^2}$ be the unit round metric and $\omega_{S^2}$ its positively
oriented area form. The **dyonic RN datum** is
$$g=-f(r)\,dx^0\otimes dx^0+f(r)^{-1}\,dr\otimes dr+r^2\gamma_{S^2}, \qquad \mathcal F=-\frac{q_e}{r^2}\,dx^0\wedge dr+q_m\omega_{S^2}.$$
Here $x^0$ and $r$ have units of metres, angles on $S^2$ are dimensionless,
and $M,q_e,q_m$ have units of metres. The metric components are dimensionless
in length coordinates; the nonzero coordinate components of $\mathcal F$ have
units inherited from their coordinate Jacobians. Use the orientation
$dx^0\wedge dr\wedge\omega_{S^2}$.

The set $J$ may have several connected components. On $\{f>0\}$ choose the
time orientation $\partial_{x^0}$; on $\{f<0\}$ choose $\partial_r$. These
are smooth timelike fields on their respective open subsets because
$g(\partial_{x^0},\partial_{x^0})=-f<0$ when $f>0$ and
$g(\partial_r,\partial_r)=f^{-1}<0$ when $f<0$. Since $f$ has no zero on
$\mathcal M_J$, this defines a smooth time orientation on the whole product.
The sphere area form and the displayed two-form are global on $S^2$.

Let $N,S$ denote the north and south poles. On
$U_N:=S^2\setminus\{S\}$ and $U_S:=S^2\setminus\{N\}$, respectively,
local potential one-forms are
$$\mathcal A_N=-\frac{q_e}{r}\,dx^0+q_m(1-\cos\theta)\,d\phi,\qquad \mathcal A_S=-\frac{q_e}{r}\,dx^0-q_m(1+\cos\theta)\,d\phi.$$
Each displayed potential extends smoothly over its named included pole:
$(1-\cos\theta)d\phi$ is smooth at $N$ and
$(1+\cos\theta)d\phi$ is smooth at $S$. Direct differentiation gives
$d\mathcal A_N=d\mathcal A_S=\mathcal F$ on the respective patches. Their
overlap difference is $2q_m\,d\phi$; it is local potential data, not a global
real gauge function on the entire sphere. The definition assumes no $U(1)$
bundle or charge quantization.

Every datum of [[def-emg-xs-harmonic-mp]] satisfies the source-free geometric Einstein-Maxwell equations of [[def-emg-xs-geometric-electrovac]]:

$$d\mathcal F_\sigma=0,\qquad d(\star_g\mathcal F_\sigma)=0,\qquad \operatorname{Ric}_{ab}=2Q_{ab}(\mathcal F_\sigma),\quad Q_{ab}(F):=F_{ac}F_b{}^c-\tfrac14g_{ab}F_{cd}F^{cd}.$$

More explicitly, with $q_H:=\sum_iH_i^2$, the only nonzero independent raised field components are $\mathcal F^{i0}_\sigma=\sigma H_i/H^2$ and the quadratic-field components are

$$\mathcal F_{\sigma,ab}\mathcal F_\sigma^{ab}=-\frac{2q_H}{H^4},\qquad Q_{00}=\frac{q_H}{2H^6},\qquad Q_{0i}=0,\qquad Q_{ij}=\frac{\delta_{ij}q_H-2H_iH_j}{2H^2}.$$

For arbitrary $M,q_e,q_m\in\mathbb R$, put $Q^2=q_e^2+q_m^2$ and
$f(r)=1-2M/r+Q^2/r^2$. On every open $J\subset(0,\infty)$ with $f\ne0$, the
dyonic RN datum of [[def-emg-xs-rn-data]] is a geometric electrovac datum of
[[def-emg-xs-geometric-electrovac]] on
$\mathbb R_{x^0}\times J\times S^2$. In particular, its global two-form is
smooth, $d\mathcal F=d(\star_g\mathcal F)=0$, and
$\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}=2Q_{ab}(\mathcal F)$ everywhere on that domain.

For arbitrary formal $c,\mu_0,G_N>0$, set $\alpha=\sqrt{4\pi G_N/(\mu_0c^4)}$, $F=\mathcal F/\alpha$, and $T_{ab}:=\mu_0^{-1}Q_g(F)_{ab}$. Then the same datum satisfies

$$dF=d(\star_gF)=0,\qquad S=0,\qquad G_{ab}=\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}=\frac{8\pi G_N}{c^4}T_{ab},$$

where $S$ is scalar curvature and $G_{ab}=\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}-\frac12Sg_{ab}$. This is the formal SI-to-geometric tensor normalization of [[lem-emg-maxwell-observer-stress]](d). It asserts neither measured parameter values nor a bundle realization for arbitrary flux. When the separate fixed-sector action hypotheses hold, $T$ is also the electromagnetic Hilbert tensor of that supplier.

Let $(M,g,N,o)$ be a smooth oriented, time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold of signature $(-,+,+,+)$; $o$ is the manifold orientation, $N$ is a smooth future timelike field, and the metric volume form is chosen to agree with $o$. Let $\nabla$ be the metric-selected connection, let $\mathcal F$ be a smooth real two-form on $M$, and use the curvature convention
$R(X,Y)Z=\nabla_X\nabla_YZ-\nabla_Y\nabla_XZ-\nabla_{[X,Y]}Z$.
Define
$$Q_{ab}(\mathcal F):=\mathcal F_{ac}\mathcal F_b{}^c-\frac14 g_{ab}\mathcal F_{cd}\mathcal F^{cd},$$
where both raised indices use $g^{-1}$. A **geometric electrovac datum with zero cosmological constant** is the tuple $(M,g,N,o,\mathcal F)$ satisfying
$$d\mathcal F=0,\qquad d(\star_g\mathcal F)=0,\qquad \operatorname{Ric}_{ab}=2Q_{ab}(\mathcal F)$$
at every point of $M$. Here $\star_g$ is the Lorentzian Hodge map determined by $g$ and $o$; on two-forms $\star_g^2=-1$. No material current, matter tensor, global potential, asymptotic flatness, positive mass, horizon, or extension condition is part of this definition.

For an oriented embedded sphere $S$ on which the integrals converge, define its geometric electric and magnetic flux parameters by
$$q_e(S):=\frac1{4\pi}\int_S\star_g\mathcal F,\qquad q_m(S):=\frac1{4\pi}\int_S\mathcal F.$$
When $M$ and the coordinates have length units, these parameters have units of length. A magnetic flux need not have a global potential; no flux quantization is included. The background Lorentzian geometry and Hodge conventions carry the countable-choice assumption $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ of their named suppliers; the algebraic identities in this definition require no additional choice principle.

derivations.claim: On $\rho>0$, $H=1+m/\rho$ is smooth and positive. Direct differentiation gives $\partial_i(\rho^{-1})=-x^i\rho^{-3}$ and $\partial_i^2(\rho^{-1})=-\rho^{-3}+3(x^i)^2\rho^{-5}$, so $\Delta_\delta H=m(-3\rho^{-3}+3\rho^2\rho^{-5})=0$; hence $H$ satisfies the hypotheses of [F1]. The map $\rho\mapsto R=\rho+m$ has smooth inverse $\rho=R-m$ on the stated open intervals and derivative $1$, so it is a diffeomorphism. Since $H=R/(R-m)$, we have $H^{-1}=1-m/R$ and $d\rho=dR$. Substitution into [F1] gives $g=-(1-m/R)^2(dx^0)^2+(1-m/R)^{-2}dR^2+R^2\gamma_{S^2}$, because the sphere coefficient is $H^2\rho^2=R^2$ and the radial coefficient is $H^2=(1-m/R)^{-2}$.

The potential transforms as $\mathcal A_\sigma=\sigma((R-m)/R-1)dx^0=-\sigma mR^{-1}dx^0$. Differentiating gives $\mathcal F_\sigma=-\sigma mR^{-2}dx^0\wedge dR$, which is exactly [F2] with $q_e=\sigma m$ and $q_m=0$. The coordinate map preserves the displayed orientation, and both future fields point along the positive $x^0$ direction on $R>m$.

We have $M=m>0$, $|q_e|=m=M$, and $q_m=0$. Thus the RN parameter relation is extremal, and $f(R)>0$ on $R>m$. The equality of the metrics in step 1.1 and two-forms in step 2.1 transfers the MP electrovac equations of [F3] to the identical RN exterior, with electrovac meaning the equations in [F4]. The conclusion does not extend the coordinate map to $\rho=0$ or $R=m$.

Let $S^2=\{n\in\mathbb R^3:|n|=1\}$ carry its induced unit round metric $\gamma_{S^2}$ and outward area form $\omega_{S^2}$. Let $L>0$ have length units. Choose either (i) $f(z)=z^2$ on an open $J\subset(0,\infty)$, or (ii) $f(z)=1+z^2$ on an open $J\subset\mathbb R$. The coordinate $z$ and $\tau$ are dimensionless. On $\mathcal M_{L,f}=\mathbb R_\tau\times J_z\times S^2$, orient by $d\tau\wedge dz\wedge\omega_{S^2}$ and define

$$g_{L,f}=L^2\bigl(-f(z)d\tau^2+f(z)^{-1}dz^2+\gamma_{S^2}\bigr),\qquad \mathcal F_L=-L\,d\tau\wedge dz.$$

The smooth field $N=(L\sqrt{f})^{-1}\partial_\tau$ is unit timelike; it selects the future direction. This explicit metric-field tuple is the **Bertotti-Robinson product data** for this library. “Electrovac” refers to the equations in [[def-emg-xs-geometric-electrovac]] and is not asserted by this definition. The product has sphere radius $L$ at every base point.

Let $(M,g,N,o)$ be a smooth oriented, time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold of signature $(-,+,+,+)$; $o$ is the manifold orientation, $N$ is a smooth future timelike field, and the metric volume form is chosen to agree with $o$. Let $\nabla$ be the metric-selected connection, let $\mathcal F$ be a smooth real two-form on $M$, and use the curvature convention
$R(X,Y)Z=\nabla_X\nabla_YZ-\nabla_Y\nabla_XZ-\nabla_{[X,Y]}Z$.
Define
$$Q_{ab}(\mathcal F):=\mathcal F_{ac}\mathcal F_b{}^c-\frac14 g_{ab}\mathcal F_{cd}\mathcal F^{cd},$$
where both raised indices use $g^{-1}$. A **geometric electrovac datum with zero cosmological constant** is the tuple $(M,g,N,o,\mathcal F)$ satisfying
$$d\mathcal F=0,\qquad d(\star_g\mathcal F)=0,\qquad \operatorname{Ric}_{ab}=2Q_{ab}(\mathcal F)$$
at every point of $M$. Here $\star_g$ is the Lorentzian Hodge map determined by $g$ and $o$; on two-forms $\star_g^2=-1$. No material current, matter tensor, global potential, asymptotic flatness, positive mass, horizon, or extension condition is part of this definition.

For an oriented embedded sphere $S$ on which the integrals converge, define its geometric electric and magnetic flux parameters by
$$q_e(S):=\frac1{4\pi}\int_S\star_g\mathcal F,\qquad q_m(S):=\frac1{4\pi}\int_S\mathcal F.$$
When $M$ and the coordinates have length units, these parameters have units of length. A magnetic flux need not have a global potential; no flux quantization is included. The background Lorentzian geometry and Hodge conventions carry the countable-choice assumption $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ of their named suppliers; the algebraic identities in this definition require no additional choice principle.

Let $(M,g,N,o)$ be the smooth, boundaryless, oriented and time-oriented
Lorentzian four-manifold of [[def-emg-lorentzian-forms]], with signature
$(-,+,+,+)$, metric-selected connection $\nabla$ and oriented metric volume
form $\mathrm{vol}_g$. Let $F\in\Omega^2(M)$ be a smooth real two-form and
$j\in\Gamma(TM)$ a smooth vector field. Fix constants $\mu_0>0$ and $c>0$;
$\mu_0$ is a real coefficient here, and $c$ is the positive coordinate
conversion in $x^0=ct$ of [[def-emg-lorentzian-forms]]. Assume the mathematical
field equations

$$dF=0,\qquad \nabla_aF^{ab}=-\mu_0j^b.$$

The equations are conditional hypotheses, not physical postulates in this
mathematical item. Define $v\in\Gamma(TM)$ by $v^b:=\nabla_aF^{ab}$ and
define the current three-form by $\iota_j\mathrm{vol}_g$, the contraction
specified in [[def-gr-metric-volume-form-and-current-flux]]. Then:

**(a) Sign identity.** On $M$,

$$d(\star_gF)=-\iota_v\mathrm{vol}_g.$$

Consequently the sourced equation is equivalently

$$\nabla_aF^{ab}=-\mu_0j^b\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad d(\star_gF)=\mu_0\iota_j\mathrm{vol}_g.$$

**(b) Current conservation.** Either equivalent sourced equation implies
$\nabla_aj^a=0$. This conclusion requires the sourced equation and $\mu_0>0$;
it does not require $dF=0$.

**(c) Local component check.** At any $p\in M$, choose a positively oriented
point-normal chart supplied by
[[thm-gr-point-normal-and-exponential-coordinate-charts]]. In that chart,
write $E_i(x):=-cF_{0i}(x)$ and
$B_i(x):=\frac12\epsilon_{ijk}F_{jk}(x)$, where $\epsilon_{123}=+1$ and
$\epsilon_{ijk}$ is alternating. These are local component abbreviations in
the chosen chart, not global observer fields. With
$\operatorname{div}E:=\partial_iE_i$,
$(\operatorname{curl}E)_k:=\epsilon_{kij}\partial_iE_j$, and similarly
for $B$, the pointwise component identities are

$$v^0=-\frac{1}{c}\operatorname{div}E,\qquad v^k=\frac{1}{c^2}\partial_tE_k-(\operatorname{curl}B)_k,$$

$$ (d\star_gF)_{123}=\frac{1}{c}\operatorname{div}E,\qquad (d\star_gF)_{0ij}=\epsilon_{ijk}\left(\frac{1}{c^2}\partial_tE_k-(\operatorname{curl}B)_k\right),$$

$$ (dF)_{123}=\operatorname{div}B,\qquad (dF)_{0ij}=\frac{\epsilon_{ijk}}{c}\left(\partial_tB_k+(\operatorname{curl}E)_k\right),$$

where $\partial_t:=c\,\partial_0$. The equations are pointwise identities
in normal coordinates; they do not assert that these component abbreviations
form global three-vector fields on curved spacetime.

On an open flat Minkowski domain with a fixed inertial Cartesian chart
$x^0=ct$, define $\rho:=j^0/c$, $J^i:=j^i$, and
$\epsilon_0:=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$. The same component formulas at every point give

$$\operatorname{div}E=\frac{\rho}{\epsilon_0},\qquad \operatorname{curl}B-\frac{1}{c^2}\partial_tE=\mu_0J,\qquad \operatorname{div}B=0,\qquad \partial_tB+\operatorname{curl}E=0.$$

These are a coordinate reduction of the stated tensor and form equations, not
claims that the smooth fields describe an experiment.

Let $M$ be a smooth four-manifold without boundary and let $g$ be a smooth
symmetric covariant $2$-tensor field on $M$ such that $g_p$ is nondegenerate at
every $p\in M$ ([[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]]). Assume
$\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ for the canonical tangent-bundle smooth structure
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-smooth-vector-field-as-a-tangent-bundle-section]]).
For this general metric define $\flat_p(v):=g_p(v,\cdot)$,
$\sharp_p:=\flat_p^{-1}$, and
$g_p^{-1}(\alpha,\beta):=g_p(\sharp_p\alpha,\sharp_p\beta)$.
Nondegeneracy makes $\flat_p$ injective and hence invertible between the
four-dimensional tangent space and its dual. In a chart, $g^{ab}$ are the
entries of the inverse matrix of $(g_{ab})$. These definitions agree with
[[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]] in its Lorentzian scope.
Here and below repeated upper/lower indices are summed over $0,1,2,3$.
This holds in particular
when $(M,g,N)$ is a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold and $g$ is
its metric ([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]). For smooth local vector fields
$X,Y,Z$ put

$$K(X,Y,Z):=X\bigl(g(Y,Z)\bigr)+Y\bigl(g(Z,X)\bigr)-Z\bigl(g(X,Y)\bigr)+g([X,Y],Z)+g([Z,X],Y)-g([Y,Z],X),$$

with brackets as in [[def-lie-bracket-of-smooth-vector-fields]].

**(a) Existence and formulas.** There is exactly one affine connection
$\nabla$ on $M$ ([[def-affine-connection-on-a-smooth-manifold]]) satisfying

$$2g(\nabla_XY,Z)=K(X,Y,Z)\qquad\text{for all smooth local }X,Y,Z .$$

It is torsion-free and $g$-compatible, so it is a metric-selected connection
for $(M,g)$, meaning torsion-free and satisfying
$Xg(Y,Z)=g(\nabla_XY,Z)+g(Y,\nabla_XZ)$ for smooth local fields
(the conditions of [[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]] extended here to
nondegenerate $g$); in every smooth chart its
Christoffel symbols are

$$\Gamma^a{}_{bc}=\tfrac12\,g^{ad}\bigl(\partial_bg_{dc}+\partial_cg_{bd}-\partial_dg_{bc}\bigr),$$

with $g^{ad}$ the inverse-metric components defined above
([[def-christoffel-symbols-of-an-affine-connection]]).

**(b) Uniqueness.** If an affine connection $\nabla'$ on $M$ is torsion-free
and $g$-compatible, then $\nabla'=\nabla$. Consequently the class
$\operatorname{LC}(M,g)$ of metric-selected connections has exactly one
element; it is the **Levi–Civita connection** of $g$.

**(c) Induced derivative on tensor fields.** Let $\nabla^*$ be the dual
connection on $T^*M$ and let the product connection of
[[def-product-connection-on-tensor-and-hom-bundles]] act on
$T^r_sM:=(TM)^{\otimes r}\otimes(T^*M)^{\otimes s}$, for integers $r,s\ge0$,
constructed by [[lem-finite-tensor-products-of-smooth-vector-bundles]]. A
type $(r,s)$ tensor at $p$ is a multilinear map
$(T_p^*M)^r\times(T_pM)^s\to\mathbb R$
([[def-type-r-s-tensor-on-a-finite-dimensional-vector-space]]); a smooth
tensor field is a section with smooth coefficients in each local product
frame. The empty product is the scalar line. Its chart components are
$T^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s}=T(dx^{a_1},\ldots,dx^{a_r},\partial_{b_1},\ldots,\partial_{b_s})$,
where $dx^a$ is dual to $\partial_a$. This agrees with
[[def-gr-tensor-fields-and-components]] in the Lorentzian case. Put
$T^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s;c}:=(\nabla_{\partial_c}T)^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s}$.
Then, in every smooth chart, for
every smooth tensor field $T$ of type $(r,s)$,

$$T^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s;c}=\partial_cT^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s}+\sum_{i=1}^{r}\Gamma^{a_i}{}_{dc}\,T^{a_1\cdots d\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s}-\sum_{j=1}^{s}\Gamma^{d}{}_{b_jc}\,T^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots d\cdots b_s},$$

where the slot marked $d$ replaces the named index; this derivative commutes
with every contraction in the sense of [[def-contraction-of-a-mixed-tensor]],
and it annihilates the metric and the inverse metric:

$$g_{ab;c}=0,\qquad g^{ab}{}_{;c}=0 .$$

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]) with metric-selected connection
$\nabla$ ([[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]]), whose existence and
uniqueness are supplied by
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]; that theorem also
extends $\nabla$ to a derivative on tensor fields commuting with contractions
and annihilating $g$ and $g^{-1}$. Let $U\subseteq M$ be open and let
$X,Y,Z$ be smooth vector fields on $U$; brackets are those of
[[def-lie-bracket-of-smooth-vector-fields]], and contractions those of
[[def-contraction-of-a-mixed-tensor]].

**(a) The curvature operator.** The **curvature operator** of $\nabla$ is the
assignment

$$R(X,Y)Z:=\nabla_X\nabla_YZ-\nabla_Y\nabla_XZ-\nabla_{[X,Y]}Z .$$

The right-hand side is a smooth vector field on $U$: $\nabla_YZ$ is smooth
because $\nabla$ is an affine connection
([[def-affine-connection-on-a-smooth-manifold]]), $[X,Y]$ is smooth, and
$\nabla_X(\cdot)$ and $\nabla_{[X,Y]}(\cdot)$ preserve smoothness. The
assignment is defined for the given smooth fields; that its value at a point
depends only on the values of $X,Y,Z$ at that point, so that $R$ is a smooth
tensor field of type $(1,3)$, is the content of
[[thm-gr-curvature-tensoriality-and-coordinate-formula]] clause (a), and
likewise the algebraic symmetries used below are proved in
[[thm-gr-curvature-algebraic-symmetries]].

**(b) Component functions.** Let $(V,x)$ be a smooth chart of $M$ and let
$\Gamma^a{}_{bc}$ be the Christoffel symbols of $\nabla$ in this chart,
characterized by $\nabla_{\partial_b}\partial_c=\sum_a\Gamma^a{}_{bc}\partial_a$
([[def-christoffel-symbols-of-an-affine-connection]]); the coordinate fields
commute, so $\nabla_{\partial_c}\partial_d$ and $\nabla_{\partial_d}\partial_c$
are obtained from the same symbols. The **components** of the curvature in the
chart are the smooth functions $R^a{}_{bcd}$ on $V$ defined by

$$R(\partial_c,\partial_d)\partial_b=\sum_a R^a{}_{bcd}\,\partial_a .$$

The first index is the output slot, the second is the differentiated slot and
the last two are the two directions of the loop; indices are $a,b,c,d=0,1,2,3$
and the Einstein summation convention of
[[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]] applies.

**(c) Lowered tensor, Ricci tensor, scalar curvature, Einstein tensor.** On
the chart domain define, using the inverse metric
$g^{ab}$ of [[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]],

$$R_{abcd}:=\sum_e g_{ae}R^e{}_{bcd},\qquad \operatorname{Ric}_{bd}:=\sum_{a,c}g^{ac}R_{abcd},\qquad S:=\sum_{b,d}g^{bd}\operatorname{Ric}_{bd},\qquad G_{ab}:=\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}-\tfrac12 S\,g_{ab}.$$

The fields $R_{abcd}$, $\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}$, $S$ and $G_{ab}$ are called
the **Riemann tensor with lowered indices**, the **Ricci tensor**, the
**scalar curvature** and the **Einstein tensor** of the metric-selected
connection. Tensoriality of $R$ is proved in
[[thm-gr-curvature-tensoriality-and-coordinate-formula]] clause (a).
Lowering its output slot with the smooth metric and contracting with the
smooth inverse metric are intrinsic tensor operations
([[def-gr-tensor-fields-and-components]] clauses (b)-(c),
[[def-contraction-of-a-mixed-tensor]]). Thus these formulas give smooth
fields of types $(0,4)$, $(0,2)$, $(0,0)$ and $(0,2)$, respectively,
independent of the chart. Symmetry of $\operatorname{Ric}$ and $G$ is proved
separately in [[thm-gr-curvature-algebraic-symmetries]] clause (d).

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with
metric-selected connection $\nabla$
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]), and let $R$ be
the curvature operator of [[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]],
with components $R^a{}_{bcd}$ in a chart.

**(a) Tensoriality.** For all smooth functions $f$ on $M$ and smooth vector
fields $X,Y,Z$ on a common domain, $R(X,Y)Z=-R(Y,X)Z$ and
$$R(fX,Y)Z=fR(X,Y)Z,\qquad R(X,fY)Z=fR(X,Y)Z,\qquad R(X,Y)(fZ)=fR(X,Y)Z .$$
Consequently, for every $p\in M$, the value $R(X,Y)Z|_p$ depends only on
$X_p,Y_p,Z_p$, and $R$ is a smooth tensor field of type $(1,3)$ on $M$ whose
components in every smooth chart are the functions $R^a{}_{bcd}$ of
[[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]] clause (b).

**(b) Coordinate formula.** In every smooth chart $(U,x)$ with Christoffel
symbols $\Gamma^a{}_{bc}$ of $\nabla$
([[def-christoffel-symbols-of-an-affine-connection]]),
$$R^a{}_{bcd}=\partial_c\Gamma^a{}_{db}-\partial_d\Gamma^a{}_{cb} +\sum_e\bigl(\Gamma^a{}_{ce}\Gamma^e{}_{db}-\Gamma^a{}_{de}\Gamma^e{}_{cb}\bigr)$$
on $U$, for all $a,b,c,d\in\{0,1,2,3\}$.

$$R_{abcd}(p)=\tfrac12\bigl(g_{ad,bc}+g_{bc,ad}-g_{bd,ac}-g_{ac,bd}\bigr)(p) .$$
Equivalently, $R^a{}_{bcd}(p)=\tfrac12\,g^{ae}(p)\bigl(\partial_b\partial_cg_{ed}
+\partial_e\partial_dg_{bc}-\partial_e\partial_cg_{bd}-\partial_b\partial_dg_{ec}\bigr)(p)$.

derivations.claim: On the two-dimensional base, the inverse metric components are $g^{\tau\tau}=-1/(L^2f)$ and $g^{zz}=f/L^2$. Applying the Christoffel formula [F4] gives, apart from lower-index symmetry, $\Gamma^\tau{}_{\tau z}=f'/(2f)$, $\Gamma^z{}_{\tau\tau}=ff'/2$, and $\Gamma^z{}_{zz}=-f'/(2f)$. Their traces $\Gamma^a{}_{\tau a}$ and $\Gamma^a{}_{za}$ are zero. Substitution in the coordinate curvature formula [F6] and the Ricci contraction [F5], with convention [F2], gives $\operatorname{Ric}_{\tau\tau}=\partial_z(ff'/2)-2(f'/2f)(ff'/2)=ff''/2$; similarly $\operatorname{Ric}_{zz}=\partial_z(-f'/2f)-\{(f'/2f)^2+(-f'/2f)^2\}=-f''/(2f)$, and $\operatorname{Ric}_{\tau z}=0$. Since $f''=2$, these are $f$ and $-1/f$, respectively, which equal $-L^{-2}$ times the corresponding components of the base metric.

For the unit sphere metric $d\theta^2+\sin^2\theta\,d\phi^2$, the Christoffel formula [F4] gives the only nonzero symbols $\Gamma^\theta{}_{\phi\phi}=-\sin\theta\cos\theta$ and $\Gamma^\phi{}_{\theta\phi}=\Gamma^\phi{}_{\phi\theta}=\cot\theta$. The coordinate curvature formula [F6] and contraction [F5] give $\operatorname{Ric}_{\theta\theta}=-\partial_\theta\cot\theta-\cot^2\theta=1$ and $\operatorname{Ric}_{\phi\phi}=\partial_\theta(-\sin\theta\cos\theta)-\cos^2\theta+2\cos^2\theta=\sin^2\theta$; the mixed component is zero. Scaling the sphere metric by the constant $L^2$ leaves its connection unchanged, so in the orthonormal coframe of the Statement its Ricci entries are $L^{-2},L^{-2}$. The product metric has no mixed Christoffel symbols because each factor coefficient depends only on its own factor coordinates; hence its mixed Ricci entries vanish.

The field is constant in $(\tau,z)$ and has only $\mathcal F_{\tau z}=-L$ and $\mathcal F_{z\tau}=L$. Thus $d\mathcal F=0$. The determinant satisfies $\sqrt{|\det g|}=L^4\sin\theta$, and raising indices gives $\mathcal F^{\tau z}=L^{-3}$ and $\mathcal F^{z\tau}=-L^{-3}$. In $\nabla_a\mathcal F^{ab}=\partial_a\mathcal F^{ab}+\Gamma^a{}_{ac}\mathcal F^{cb}+\Gamma^b{}_{ac}\mathcal F^{ac}$, the last term vanishes by symmetry of the connection and antisymmetry of the field. For $b=\tau,z$, the only derivative terms are $\partial_z\mathcal F^{z\tau}$ and $\partial_\tau\mathcal F^{\tau z}$, both zero; their trace terms vanish because $\Gamma^a{}_{a\tau}=\Gamma^a{}_{az}=0$ from the base Christoffels and the product has no mixed symbols. For $b=\theta,\phi$, all $\mathcal F^{ab}$ vanish. Hence $\nabla_a\mathcal F^{ab}=0$; [F3] gives $d(\star_g\mathcal F)=0$.

In the orthonormal coframe, $\mathcal F_L=-L^{-1}e^0\wedge e^1$, so $\mathcal F_{AB}\mathcal F^{AB}=-2/L^2$. Direct contraction in signature $(-,+,+,+)$ gives $Q_{AB}=\frac1{2L^2}\operatorname{diag}(1,-1,1,1)_{AB}$: the electric pair contributes $+1/(2L^2)$ to the time entry and $-1/(2L^2)$ to the radial entry, while the trace term contributes $+1/(2L^2)$ to each sphere entry. Steps 1.1 and 2.1 give the base and sphere Ricci tensors, so $\operatorname{Ric}=2Q$. Together with the Maxwell equations in step 3.1 this is the full definition of a geometric electrovac datum.

Let $M,q_e,q_m\in\mathbb R$ be length parameters and put
$Q^2:=q_e^2+q_m^2$. Let $J\subset(0,\infty)$ be open and require
$$f(r):=1-\frac{2M}{r}+\frac{Q^2}{r^2}\ne0\qquad(r\in J).$$
On the smooth product $\mathcal M_J:=\mathbb R_{x^0}\times J_r\times S^2$,
let $\gamma_{S^2}$ be the unit round metric and $\omega_{S^2}$ its positively
oriented area form. The **dyonic RN datum** is
$$g=-f(r)\,dx^0\otimes dx^0+f(r)^{-1}\,dr\otimes dr+r^2\gamma_{S^2}, \qquad \mathcal F=-\frac{q_e}{r^2}\,dx^0\wedge dr+q_m\omega_{S^2}.$$
Here $x^0$ and $r$ have units of metres, angles on $S^2$ are dimensionless,
and $M,q_e,q_m$ have units of metres. The metric components are dimensionless
in length coordinates; the nonzero coordinate components of $\mathcal F$ have
units inherited from their coordinate Jacobians. Use the orientation
$dx^0\wedge dr\wedge\omega_{S^2}$.

The set $J$ may have several connected components. On $\{f>0\}$ choose the
time orientation $\partial_{x^0}$; on $\{f<0\}$ choose $\partial_r$. These
are smooth timelike fields on their respective open subsets because
$g(\partial_{x^0},\partial_{x^0})=-f<0$ when $f>0$ and
$g(\partial_r,\partial_r)=f^{-1}<0$ when $f<0$. Since $f$ has no zero on
$\mathcal M_J$, this defines a smooth time orientation on the whole product.
The sphere area form and the displayed two-form are global on $S^2$.

Let $N,S$ denote the north and south poles. On
$U_N:=S^2\setminus\{S\}$ and $U_S:=S^2\setminus\{N\}$, respectively,
local potential one-forms are
$$\mathcal A_N=-\frac{q_e}{r}\,dx^0+q_m(1-\cos\theta)\,d\phi,\qquad \mathcal A_S=-\frac{q_e}{r}\,dx^0-q_m(1+\cos\theta)\,d\phi.$$
Each displayed potential extends smoothly over its named included pole:
$(1-\cos\theta)d\phi$ is smooth at $N$ and
$(1+\cos\theta)d\phi$ is smooth at $S$. Direct differentiation gives
$d\mathcal A_N=d\mathcal A_S=\mathcal F$ on the respective patches. Their
overlap difference is $2q_m\,d\phi$; it is local potential data, not a global
real gauge function on the entire sphere. The definition assumes no $U(1)$
bundle or charge quantization.

For arbitrary $M,q_e,q_m\in\mathbb R$, put $Q^2=q_e^2+q_m^2$ and
$f(r)=1-2M/r+Q^2/r^2$. On every open $J\subset(0,\infty)$ with $f\ne0$, the
dyonic RN datum of [[def-emg-xs-rn-data]] is a geometric electrovac datum of
[[def-emg-xs-geometric-electrovac]] on
$\mathbb R_{x^0}\times J\times S^2$. In particular, its global two-form is
smooth, $d\mathcal F=d(\star_g\mathcal F)=0$, and
$\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}=2Q_{ab}(\mathcal F)$ everywhere on that domain.

For arbitrary formal $c,\mu_0,G_N>0$, set $\alpha=\sqrt{4\pi G_N/(\mu_0c^4)}$, $F=\mathcal F/\alpha$, and $T_{ab}:=\mu_0^{-1}Q_g(F)_{ab}$. Then the same datum satisfies

$$dF=d(\star_gF)=0,\qquad S=0,\qquad G_{ab}=\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}=\frac{8\pi G_N}{c^4}T_{ab},$$

where $S$ is scalar curvature and $G_{ab}=\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}-\frac12Sg_{ab}$. This is the formal SI-to-geometric tensor normalization of [[lem-emg-maxwell-observer-stress]](d). It asserts neither measured parameter values nor a bundle realization for arbitrary flux. When the separate fixed-sector action hypotheses hold, $T$ is also the electromagnetic Hilbert tensor of that supplier.

Let $S^2=\{n\in\mathbb R^3:|n|=1\}$ carry its induced unit round metric $\gamma_{S^2}$ and outward area form $\omega_{S^2}$. Let $L>0$ have length units. Choose either (i) $f(z)=z^2$ on an open $J\subset(0,\infty)$, or (ii) $f(z)=1+z^2$ on an open $J\subset\mathbb R$. The coordinate $z$ and $\tau$ are dimensionless. On $\mathcal M_{L,f}=\mathbb R_\tau\times J_z\times S^2$, orient by $d\tau\wedge dz\wedge\omega_{S^2}$ and define

$$g_{L,f}=L^2\bigl(-f(z)d\tau^2+f(z)^{-1}dz^2+\gamma_{S^2}\bigr),\qquad \mathcal F_L=-L\,d\tau\wedge dz.$$

The smooth field $N=(L\sqrt{f})^{-1}\partial_\tau$ is unit timelike; it selects the future direction. This explicit metric-field tuple is the **Bertotti-Robinson product data** for this library. “Electrovac” refers to the equations in [[def-emg-xs-geometric-electrovac]] and is not asserted by this definition. The product has sphere radius $L$ at every base point.

Every datum in [[def-emg-xs-br-products]] is a geometric electrovac datum of [[def-emg-xs-geometric-electrovac]]. With the oriented orthonormal coframe

$$e^0=L\sqrt f\,d\tau,\quad e^1=L f^{-1/2}dz,\quad e^2=L\,d\theta,\quad e^3=L\sin\theta\,d\phi,$$

the Ricci and quadratic Maxwell tensors are

$$\operatorname{Ric}_{AB}=L^{-2}\operatorname{diag}(1,-1,1,1)_{AB},\qquad Q_{AB}(\mathcal F_L)=\frac1{2L^2}\operatorname{diag}(1,-1,1,1)_{AB}.$$

All mixed base-sphere entries vanish. The statement is on the chosen open chart domains; it makes no maximal-extension or asymptotic-flatness claim.

Let $(M,g,N,o)$ be a smooth oriented, time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold of signature $(-,+,+,+)$; $o$ is the manifold orientation, $N$ is a smooth future timelike field, and the metric volume form is chosen to agree with $o$. Let $\nabla$ be the metric-selected connection, let $\mathcal F$ be a smooth real two-form on $M$, and use the curvature convention
$R(X,Y)Z=\nabla_X\nabla_YZ-\nabla_Y\nabla_XZ-\nabla_{[X,Y]}Z$.
Define
$$Q_{ab}(\mathcal F):=\mathcal F_{ac}\mathcal F_b{}^c-\frac14 g_{ab}\mathcal F_{cd}\mathcal F^{cd},$$
where both raised indices use $g^{-1}$. A **geometric electrovac datum with zero cosmological constant** is the tuple $(M,g,N,o,\mathcal F)$ satisfying
$$d\mathcal F=0,\qquad d(\star_g\mathcal F)=0,\qquad \operatorname{Ric}_{ab}=2Q_{ab}(\mathcal F)$$
at every point of $M$. Here $\star_g$ is the Lorentzian Hodge map determined by $g$ and $o$; on two-forms $\star_g^2=-1$. No material current, matter tensor, global potential, asymptotic flatness, positive mass, horizon, or extension condition is part of this definition.

For an oriented embedded sphere $S$ on which the integrals converge, define its geometric electric and magnetic flux parameters by
$$q_e(S):=\frac1{4\pi}\int_S\star_g\mathcal F,\qquad q_m(S):=\frac1{4\pi}\int_S\mathcal F.$$
When $M$ and the coordinates have length units, these parameters have units of length. A magnetic flux need not have a global potential; no flux quantization is included. The background Lorentzian geometry and Hodge conventions carry the countable-choice assumption $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ of their named suppliers; the algebraic identities in this definition require no additional choice principle.

derivations.claim: The map $\Phi_\lambda$ is a diffeomorphism from $\mathbb R_T\times(0,\infty)_R\times S^2$ onto the RN exterior $r>L$, since $x^0=T/\lambda$ and $r=L+\lambda R$ have smooth inverses. Its pullback satisfies $dx^0=dT/\lambda$ and $dr=\lambda dR$, while $f(r)=(1-L/r)^2=\lambda^2R^2/(L+\lambda R)^2$. Substitution into the RN metric in [F1] gives the displayed $g_\lambda$. The starting RN datum is a geometric electrovac by the first clause of [F2]; the claim here is the exact coordinate pullback and its limit.
The RN two-form in [F1] pulls back to $-\frac{L}{(L+\lambda R)^2}\frac{dT}{\lambda}\wedge(\lambda dR)=-\frac{L}{(L+\lambda R)^2}dT\wedge dR$, which is the displayed $\mathcal F_\lambda$.

At $\lambda=0$ the coefficient formulas in the Statement are smooth for $R>0$. Fix any compact subset $K$ of $\mathbb R_T\times(0,\infty)_R\times S^2$ and choose a finite smooth atlas on its sphere projection. In each chart, $R$ is bounded below by a positive number and $L+\lambda R\ge L$ for $0\le\lambda\le1$. Every coordinate derivative of every displayed coefficient is therefore a continuous function of $(\lambda,T,R,\theta,\phi)$ on a compact set containing $\{0\}\times K$; uniform continuity implies that each such derivative converges uniformly on $K$ to its value at $\lambda=0$. Since this holds for every derivative order and the atlas is finite, the convergence is $C^\infty_{\rm loc}$.

Substituting $T=L\tau$ and $R=Lz$ into $g_0,\mathcal F_0$ gives $L^2(-z^2d\tau^2+z^{-2}dz^2+\gamma_{S^2})$ and $-L\,d\tau\wedge dz$, exactly [F3] with $f=z^2$. By [F4] this limiting product satisfies the equations defined in [F5]. This identification is on $z>0$ only and does not add a horizon chart.

Let $(M,g,N,o)$ be the smooth, boundaryless, oriented and time-oriented
Lorentzian four-manifold of [[def-emg-lorentzian-forms]], with signature
$(-,+,+,+)$, metric-selected connection $\nabla$ and oriented metric volume
form $\mathrm{vol}_g$. Let $F\in\Omega^2(M)$ be a smooth real two-form and
$j\in\Gamma(TM)$ a smooth vector field. Fix constants $\mu_0>0$ and $c>0$;
$\mu_0$ is a real coefficient here, and $c$ is the positive coordinate
conversion in $x^0=ct$ of [[def-emg-lorentzian-forms]]. Assume the mathematical
field equations

$$dF=0,\qquad \nabla_aF^{ab}=-\mu_0j^b.$$

The equations are conditional hypotheses, not physical postulates in this
mathematical item. Define $v\in\Gamma(TM)$ by $v^b:=\nabla_aF^{ab}$ and
define the current three-form by $\iota_j\mathrm{vol}_g$, the contraction
specified in [[def-gr-metric-volume-form-and-current-flux]]. Then:

**(a) Sign identity.** On $M$,

$$d(\star_gF)=-\iota_v\mathrm{vol}_g.$$

Consequently the sourced equation is equivalently

$$\nabla_aF^{ab}=-\mu_0j^b\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad d(\star_gF)=\mu_0\iota_j\mathrm{vol}_g.$$

**(b) Current conservation.** Either equivalent sourced equation implies
$\nabla_aj^a=0$. This conclusion requires the sourced equation and $\mu_0>0$;
it does not require $dF=0$.

**(c) Local component check.** At any $p\in M$, choose a positively oriented
point-normal chart supplied by
[[thm-gr-point-normal-and-exponential-coordinate-charts]]. In that chart,
write $E_i(x):=-cF_{0i}(x)$ and
$B_i(x):=\frac12\epsilon_{ijk}F_{jk}(x)$, where $\epsilon_{123}=+1$ and
$\epsilon_{ijk}$ is alternating. These are local component abbreviations in
the chosen chart, not global observer fields. With
$\operatorname{div}E:=\partial_iE_i$,
$(\operatorname{curl}E)_k:=\epsilon_{kij}\partial_iE_j$, and similarly
for $B$, the pointwise component identities are

$$v^0=-\frac{1}{c}\operatorname{div}E,\qquad v^k=\frac{1}{c^2}\partial_tE_k-(\operatorname{curl}B)_k,$$

$$ (d\star_gF)_{123}=\frac{1}{c}\operatorname{div}E,\qquad (d\star_gF)_{0ij}=\epsilon_{ijk}\left(\frac{1}{c^2}\partial_tE_k-(\operatorname{curl}B)_k\right),$$

$$ (dF)_{123}=\operatorname{div}B,\qquad (dF)_{0ij}=\frac{\epsilon_{ijk}}{c}\left(\partial_tB_k+(\operatorname{curl}E)_k\right),$$

where $\partial_t:=c\,\partial_0$. The equations are pointwise identities
in normal coordinates; they do not assert that these component abbreviations
form global three-vector fields on curved spacetime.

On an open flat Minkowski domain with a fixed inertial Cartesian chart
$x^0=ct$, define $\rho:=j^0/c$, $J^i:=j^i$, and
$\epsilon_0:=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$. The same component formulas at every point give

$$\operatorname{div}E=\frac{\rho}{\epsilon_0},\qquad \operatorname{curl}B-\frac{1}{c^2}\partial_tE=\mu_0J,\qquad \operatorname{div}B=0,\qquad \partial_tB+\operatorname{curl}E=0.$$

These are a coordinate reduction of the stated tensor and form equations, not
claims that the smooth fields describe an experiment.

Let $M$ be a smooth four-manifold without boundary and let $g$ be a smooth
symmetric covariant $2$-tensor field on $M$ such that $g_p$ is nondegenerate at
every $p\in M$ ([[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]]). Assume
$\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ for the canonical tangent-bundle smooth structure
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-smooth-vector-field-as-a-tangent-bundle-section]]).
For this general metric define $\flat_p(v):=g_p(v,\cdot)$,
$\sharp_p:=\flat_p^{-1}$, and
$g_p^{-1}(\alpha,\beta):=g_p(\sharp_p\alpha,\sharp_p\beta)$.
Nondegeneracy makes $\flat_p$ injective and hence invertible between the
four-dimensional tangent space and its dual. In a chart, $g^{ab}$ are the
entries of the inverse matrix of $(g_{ab})$. These definitions agree with
[[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]] in its Lorentzian scope.
Here and below repeated upper/lower indices are summed over $0,1,2,3$.
This holds in particular
when $(M,g,N)$ is a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold and $g$ is
its metric ([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]). For smooth local vector fields
$X,Y,Z$ put

$$K(X,Y,Z):=X\bigl(g(Y,Z)\bigr)+Y\bigl(g(Z,X)\bigr)-Z\bigl(g(X,Y)\bigr)+g([X,Y],Z)+g([Z,X],Y)-g([Y,Z],X),$$

with brackets as in [[def-lie-bracket-of-smooth-vector-fields]].

**(a) Existence and formulas.** There is exactly one affine connection
$\nabla$ on $M$ ([[def-affine-connection-on-a-smooth-manifold]]) satisfying

$$2g(\nabla_XY,Z)=K(X,Y,Z)\qquad\text{for all smooth local }X,Y,Z .$$

It is torsion-free and $g$-compatible, so it is a metric-selected connection
for $(M,g)$, meaning torsion-free and satisfying
$Xg(Y,Z)=g(\nabla_XY,Z)+g(Y,\nabla_XZ)$ for smooth local fields
(the conditions of [[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]] extended here to
nondegenerate $g$); in every smooth chart its
Christoffel symbols are

$$\Gamma^a{}_{bc}=\tfrac12\,g^{ad}\bigl(\partial_bg_{dc}+\partial_cg_{bd}-\partial_dg_{bc}\bigr),$$

with $g^{ad}$ the inverse-metric components defined above
([[def-christoffel-symbols-of-an-affine-connection]]).

**(b) Uniqueness.** If an affine connection $\nabla'$ on $M$ is torsion-free
and $g$-compatible, then $\nabla'=\nabla$. Consequently the class
$\operatorname{LC}(M,g)$ of metric-selected connections has exactly one
element; it is the **Levi–Civita connection** of $g$.

**(c) Induced derivative on tensor fields.** Let $\nabla^*$ be the dual
connection on $T^*M$ and let the product connection of
[[def-product-connection-on-tensor-and-hom-bundles]] act on
$T^r_sM:=(TM)^{\otimes r}\otimes(T^*M)^{\otimes s}$, for integers $r,s\ge0$,
constructed by [[lem-finite-tensor-products-of-smooth-vector-bundles]]. A
type $(r,s)$ tensor at $p$ is a multilinear map
$(T_p^*M)^r\times(T_pM)^s\to\mathbb R$
([[def-type-r-s-tensor-on-a-finite-dimensional-vector-space]]); a smooth
tensor field is a section with smooth coefficients in each local product
frame. The empty product is the scalar line. Its chart components are
$T^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s}=T(dx^{a_1},\ldots,dx^{a_r},\partial_{b_1},\ldots,\partial_{b_s})$,
where $dx^a$ is dual to $\partial_a$. This agrees with
[[def-gr-tensor-fields-and-components]] in the Lorentzian case. Put
$T^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s;c}:=(\nabla_{\partial_c}T)^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s}$.
Then, in every smooth chart, for
every smooth tensor field $T$ of type $(r,s)$,

$$T^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s;c}=\partial_cT^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s}+\sum_{i=1}^{r}\Gamma^{a_i}{}_{dc}\,T^{a_1\cdots d\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s}-\sum_{j=1}^{s}\Gamma^{d}{}_{b_jc}\,T^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots d\cdots b_s},$$

where the slot marked $d$ replaces the named index; this derivative commutes
with every contraction in the sense of [[def-contraction-of-a-mixed-tensor]],
and it annihilates the metric and the inverse metric:

$$g_{ab;c}=0,\qquad g^{ab}{}_{;c}=0 .$$

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]) with metric-selected connection
$\nabla$ ([[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]]), whose existence and
uniqueness are supplied by
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]; that theorem also

derivations.claim: In the ordered coordinates $(u,v,x,y)$ the metric matrix has $(u,v)$ block $\begin{pmatrix}P&-1\\-1&0\end{pmatrix}$ and transverse block $I_2$. Its inverse has $g^{uv}=g^{vu}=-1$, $g^{vv}=-P$, $g^{uu}=0$, $g^{xx}=g^{yy}=1$; the determinant is $-1$. The field has only $\mathcal F_{ux}=a$ and $\mathcal F_{uy}=b$, so direct raising gives $\mathcal F^{vx}=-a$, $\mathcal F^{vy}=-b$, with $\mathcal F^{ux}=\mathcal F^{uy}=0$. Direct differentiation of $\mathcal F=a(u)du\wedge dx+b(u)du\wedge dy$ gives $d\mathcal F=0$, since each derivative term contains $du\wedge du$.

The nonzero Christoffel symbols, apart from lower-index symmetry, are $\Gamma^v{}_{uu}=-P_u/2$, $\Gamma^v{}_{ui}=-P_i/2$, and $\Gamma^i{}_{uu}=-P_i/2$ for $i\in\{x,y\}$. Substitution of the metric and inverse into [F4] gives these entries; the remaining metric derivatives vanish or lie in a constant block. Each trace $\Gamma^a{}_{ac}$ is zero. Hence $\nabla_a\mathcal F^{ab}=\partial_a\mathcal F^{ab}$, because $\Gamma^b{}_{ac}\mathcal F^{ac}=0$ by symmetry. The only nonzero raised field components have upper pair $vx$ or $vy$, are independent of $v$, and have no component with upper $u$; therefore every $\partial_a\mathcal F^{ab}=0$. By [F3], $d(\star_g\mathcal F)=0$.

The coordinate curvature and Ricci formulas [F5, F6] with the Christoffel list in step 2.1 have zero trace-derivative and trace-product terms because $\Gamma^a{}_{ac}=0$. In the last product $\Gamma^a{}_{b c}\Gamma^c{}_{a d}$, $c=u$ gives a zero second factor (no Christoffel has upper $u$), $c=v$ gives a zero first factor (no Christoffel has lower $v$), and for transverse $c=i$ a nonzero first factor requires $a=v$, making the second factor zero because it then has lower $v$. Hence that product vanishes. In the derivative term $\partial_a\Gamma^a{}_{\nu\beta}$, the only nonzero derivatives are $\partial_x\Gamma^x{}_{uu}=-P_{xx}/2$ and $\partial_y\Gamma^y{}_{uu}=-P_{yy}/2$. Thus $\operatorname{Ric}_{uu}=-(P_{xx}+P_{yy})/2$ and every other Ricci component is zero. From [F1], $P_{xx}+P_{yy}=-4(a^2+b^2)+h_{xx}+h_{yy}=-4(a^2+b^2)$, giving the stated Ricci component.

([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-smooth-vector-field-as-a-tangent-bundle-section]]).

[[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]] in its Lorentzian scope.

Let $(M,g,N,o)$ be a smooth oriented, time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold of signature $(-,+,+,+)$; $o$ is the manifold orientation, $N$ is a smooth future timelike field, and the metric volume form is chosen to agree with $o$. Let $\nabla$ be the metric-selected connection, let $\mathcal F$ be a smooth real two-form on $M$, and use the curvature convention
$R(X,Y)Z=\nabla_X\nabla_YZ-\nabla_Y\nabla_XZ-\nabla_{[X,Y]}Z$.
Define
$$Q_{ab}(\mathcal F):=\mathcal F_{ac}\mathcal F_b{}^c-\frac14 g_{ab}\mathcal F_{cd}\mathcal F^{cd},$$
where both raised indices use $g^{-1}$. A **geometric electrovac datum with zero cosmological constant** is the tuple $(M,g,N,o,\mathcal F)$ satisfying
$$d\mathcal F=0,\qquad d(\star_g\mathcal F)=0,\qquad \operatorname{Ric}_{ab}=2Q_{ab}(\mathcal F)$$
at every point of $M$. Here $\star_g$ is the Lorentzian Hodge map determined by $g$ and $o$; on two-forms $\star_g^2=-1$. No material current, matter tensor, global potential, asymptotic flatness, positive mass, horizon, or extension condition is part of this definition.

For an oriented embedded sphere $S$ on which the integrals converge, define its geometric electric and magnetic flux parameters by
$$q_e(S):=\frac1{4\pi}\int_S\star_g\mathcal F,\qquad q_m(S):=\frac1{4\pi}\int_S\mathcal F.$$
When $M$ and the coordinates have length units, these parameters have units of length. A magnetic flux need not have a global potential; no flux quantization is included. The background Lorentzian geometry and Hodge conventions carry the countable-choice assumption $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ of their named suppliers; the algebraic identities in this definition require no additional choice principle.

Every candidate datum in [[def-emg-xs-null-wave]] is a smooth source-free geometric electrovac datum in the convention of [[def-emg-xs-geometric-electrovac]]. Its only nonzero Ricci component is

$$\operatorname{Ric}_{uu}=2(a(u)^2+b(u)^2),$$

and its Maxwell quadratic tensor has only $Q_{uu}=a(u)^2+b(u)^2$ nonzero. Thus $\operatorname{Ric}=2Q(\mathcal F)$ for arbitrary smooth profiles $a,b$ and every smooth transverse harmonic addition $h$ specified in the definition. No asymptotic-flatness or finite-energy assertion is included.

For every null-wave electrovac datum of [[def-emg-xs-null-wave]] and [[thm-emg-xs-null-wave-verification]],

$$\mathcal F_{ab}\mathcal F^{ab}=0,\qquad S=0,\qquad \operatorname{Ric}_{ab}\operatorname{Ric}^{ab}=0,\qquad R_{abcd}R^{abcd}=0.$$

In the displayed coordinates the only potentially nonzero independent Riemann components are

$$R_{uiuj}=-\frac12P_{ij},\qquad i,j\in\{x,y\}.$$

If $a(u_0)^2+b(u_0)^2>0$ at any $u_0$, then the Riemann tensor is nonzero there; the metric is not flat. Here $R_{abcd}$ and $S$ use the convention in [[def-emg-xs-geometric-electrovac]].

derivations.claim: The choices in [A1] satisfy the smoothness and transverse-harmonic hypotheses in [F1]. They give $P=-a_0^2(x^2+y^2)$ and $\mathcal F=a_0\,du\wedge dx$, which is nonzero. Under the definition in [F2], [F3] proves this is a smooth source-free geometric electrovac datum.

Applying [F4] gives $\mathcal F_{ab}\mathcal F^{ab}=S=\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}\operatorname{Ric}^{ab}=R_{abcd}R^{abcd}=0$. But $P_{xx}=-2a_0^2$, so $R_{uxux}=-P_{xx}/2=a_0^2\ne0$. Thus the field is nonzero and the metric is not flat although all four displayed scalar invariants vanish.
